key_concepts: Simple machines change the direction and size of forces
An inclined plane is a slanted flat surface with one end higher than the other
Inclined planes reduce effort by applying a smaller force over a longer distance
The screw and wedge are two kinds of inclined planes
A screw is an inclined plane wrapped around a cylinder
Screw threads are inclined grooves; more threads mean lower slope and less force needed
Pitch is the distance between screw threads and the tip is the pointed end
A wedge is two inclined planes joined at a common base, thick at one end and sharp at the
Cutting tools are wedges and need friction to function
An Archimedes screw lifts water when turned at an angle
Fan blades, bathtub floors, ladders, and bottle caps can act as inclined planes or screws
Input force moves an object along the plane while output force lifts it vertically
